summary:
I demonstrated two breaks; the rest of the plan is delivered and its checks have teeth.

BREAK 1 (execution-000011). Plan section 2 requires to_utc to preserve the input time unit "while removing any timezone from its dtype; the result is a naive pl.Datetime column". to_utc reuses `result.data.schema["time"]` verbatim for the output series and reads wall clocks off the aware series. Two ObservationResults built from ONE identical row (wall clock 2026-01-15 12:00:00, zone Europe/Zurich) differing only in the `time` dtype: with the naive dtype the output is naive 11:00:00 and schema-identical; with dtype Datetime('us','America/Chicago') - which ObservationResult validation accepts, observations.py:235-236 - the output dtype stays 'America/Chicago' and the value is 05:00:00, while the row is stamped '+00:00'. The four-line replacement (derive `naive_dtype` from `time_dtype.time_unit`, strip tzinfo with `dt.replace_time_zone(None)` before reading, construct the series with `naive_dtype`) makes the rejection input produce naive 11:00:00 and keeps the plan's own tests and all three gates green (execution-000030). No delivered test exercises any non-default time dtype, so nothing caught this.

BREAK 2 (execution-000027, acceptance pair execution-000028). test_to_utc_usgs_dst_boundary_uses_each_payload_offset_without_catalogue is vacuous for the code path it names. Mutating the subject so to_utc actually loads the packaged USGS catalogue via a direct `from ... import load_packaged_catalogue_artifact` prints 26258 stations rows and the test still PASSES, identically to the unmutated run - patching the name on its defining module cannot intercept a caller that bound the function object at import. Adding `monkeypatch.setattr(pl, "read_parquet"/"scan_parquet", catalogue_probe)` keeps the built artifact green (4 passed) and reddens the mutation with `AssertionError: to_utc consulted the catalogue` (execution-000029).

EVERYTHING ELSE HOLDS, and I proved it can detect a known problem before saying so. Six single-property mutations each reddened exactly the assertions claiming that property: IANA rules replaced by a fixed +00:00 (execution-000013), refusal removed (execution-000014), the unknown preflight moved after the conversion loop while keeping the identical message (execution-000017 - so atomicity, not just refusal, is measured), the negative-offset sign flip (execution-000018), one zone reused for every row (execution-000019), and the __init__ re-export deleted (execution-000020). Focused acceptance set: 5 passed (execution-000004). Whole suite through the harness in three disjoint partitions totalling 1626 passed / 2 skipped (execution-000034/35/36), matching the plan's 1622 baseline plus exactly four new tests and the two pre-existing folium skips; the direct worktree run agrees. ruff format --check, ruff check, and ty check src are all clean (execution-000021). The diff is exactly the five write-set paths with no noqa/type-ignore/marker and no touch to pyproject.toml, uv.lock, .pce/repository-contract.json, ruff/ty config, or tests/typecheck/nominal_window_misuse.py; one conventional commit with the exact required subject and no footer, no tag, version still 0.1.49, pr-body.md present and untracked (execution-000022, execution-000023). The DST fixture is byte-identical to the plan text (execution-000031), the only edited pre-existing assertion is the one plan section 4 authorises, and pr-body.md's single stated figure matches my measurement - though its 'naive UTC' claim is exactly what break 1 falsifies. The worktree is left tracked-clean (execution-000037).
